title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why does this track state its exclusions in the first minute?
options: To set expectations about the time commitment
Because the exclusions are the product — most material sold to this audience spends half its runtime on remedial content written for a broad HR population and priced for a senior one
Because the excluded topics are covered in optional supplementary material
Because fundamentals are outside the scope of any 301 track
questions.explanation: For this audience specifically, refusing to re-teach the basics is a credibility move, and it is true. If you need the fundamentals, 101 and 201 will do it better than a course pretending to serve executives.

questions.prompt: How does the module handle the survey evidence for the credibility chain? `[V]`
options: It presents it as the anchor finding supporting the module's argument
It states the sample, the publisher's interest, and the absence of causal direction — then sets it aside and argues from the mechanism instead
It dismisses the finding as unreliable and does not report it
It presents it alongside a contradicting study without resolving the tension
questions.explanation: Both halves matter. Leading on a citation this audience can dismiss in one line would have cost more than the number was worth — and doing so in the first module would have discredited everything after it.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes executive-altitude practice from ordinary executive AI use?
options: It uses more capable models with longer context windows
It is performed personally rather than through an assistant
The model is aimed at your reasoning rather than your output — none of the three uses produces a deliverable
It focuses on strategic rather than operational questions
questions.explanation: Delegated drafting is useful and develops no judgment, because the output is something you were going to review anyway. B is close but incomplete: doing ordinary drafting yourself is still ordinary drafting.

questions.prompt: Why is catching a model being confidently wrong in your own domain described as non-substitutable?
options: Because it demonstrates the limits of the specific model being used

Because being told that models are confidently wrong is different knowledge from knowing what it feels like when one is wrong about something you know well — and the second is what you need in a procurement conversation
Because domain-specific errors are more common than general ones
Because it establishes a baseline error rate for that model
questions.explanation: It is the difference between a briefing and judgment, and it is why the chain's first link cannot be delegated.

questions.prompt: What are the two mechanisms by which delegated fluency fails?
options: Slower decision cycles and increased vendor dependency
You lose the ability to interrogate what you are told, and your own errors stop being corrected because nobody above you is positioned to catch them
Loss of technical credibility with the IT function and reduced budget authority
Over-reliance on a single adviser and inconsistent policy application
questions.explanation: The second is the one specific to your seat. Everyone else has somebody who might catch a mistaken belief about what AI can do; a mistaken CPO propagates it downward into procurement and policy unchallenged.

questions.prompt: How does the module answer the "nobody expects a CFO to do the accounting" objection?
options: By arguing that AI is more central to HR than accounting is to finance

By conceding it is real, and noting that a CFO's second-hand judgment rests on audits, standards, and regulators — an apparatus that does not yet exist for AI claims, which makes the argument time-limited rather than eternal
By pointing out that CFOs do in fact require technical accounting knowledge
By arguing the comparison fails because AI affects every function rather than one
questions.explanation: And naming it as time-limited is the honest part. When vendor claims are audited and benchmarks are independent, first-hand knowledge will stop doing work it currently has to do.

questions.prompt: Why does the track reject confidence ratings as a measure?
options: Because they are difficult to compare between organizations

Because self-reported confidence correlates with marketing exposure, temperament, and recency rather than capability — and is systematically inflated at senior levels, where admitting uncertainty reads as being behind
Because executives are less accurate self-raters than individual contributors
Because confidence changes too quickly to be tracked usefully
questions.explanation: Behaviour is checkable against a record. It does not require honesty with yourself in the abstract, only that you go and look.

questions.prompt: A learner runs their practice twice, finds it does not survive their calendar, and says precisely why. How should that be scored?
options: As an incomplete submission, since the practice was not sustained
As more useful than a report of enthusiasm, provided the account of why it failed is specific
As acceptable only if they propose an alternative practice
As evidence the practice chosen was poorly matched to their role
questions.explanation: The activity asks what happened, not what they hoped. A precise account of why a practice failed contact with a real executive week is genuinely more useful than an untested intention — and it is the honest answer this track's standard is designed to make available.
